title: Is the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 the right board for my project?
short: A small Bluetooth and Zigbee board built around TI's CC2340R52 chip. Bluetooth and Zigbee ran from TI's examples with settings changes only; RAM (36 kB) is what limits it, at least in TI's configurations as we built them. TI.com no longer sells this board; DigiKey listed it on 2026-10-08; the LP-EM-CC2340R53, with 64 kB of RAM, is the kit TI sells now, and our Thread and two-radio builds linked for its chip.

meet.what: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's CC2340R52 wireless chip: Bluetooth Low Energy, Zigbee, and Thread as a radio co-processor. It has no USB port of its own; a separate XDS110 probe clips on to power it, flash it and carry its serial port.
facts: 2.4 GHz: Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread (radio co-processor only), proprietary
TI SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK (FreeRTOS); upstream Zephyr for blink only
TI.com no longer sells it; DigiKey listed it at $34.38 on 2026-10-08. TI now sells the LP-EM-CC2340R53 ($27.50)

projects.result: Offered and downloading after four fixes; best 7.20% of the image before stalling. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Radio environment).** Cause not found

chains.why: TI's examples leave about 5.1 kB of RAM for your code
TI's examples leave 0.8 kB (router, logging on) to 10.7 kB (update client, logging off) of RAM for your code

chains.t: Two radio stacks at the same time
chains.why: TI's release notes say CC23xx chips do not support two stacks at once. TI's two-radio example for the CC2755P10, Bluetooth plus TI 15.4, moved by us to this chip, did not link. It was 2.1 kB of RAM short even before its 19.3 kB heap. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** Only that example was tried. It links for the CC2340R53 after that build's 40 kB heap is cut to 24 kB; not run

chains.t: Thread as an end device or router
chains.why: TI's configurations did not link when built with our toolchain, which is not the version TI tested. They were 7.5 to 20.7 kB of RAM short for the default builds, up to 23.8 kB with the NCP option. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** A trimmed build was not tried. They link for the CC2340R53; not run

chains.t: Thread as a radio for another computer (RCP)
chains.why: TI's ot-rcp image, driven by OpenThread on a Mac, joined a Thread network led by the LP-CC1354P10-1 and became a router. It is also the radio of our two-board border router host
chains.verdict: Yes, as the radio for a computer or another board

chains.why: TI offers no Matter build for this chip
chains.verdict: No, TI has no Matter build for this chip

chains.why: Upstream Zephyr has no Bluetooth for this board. In TI's fork, with Zephyr's C library heap set to CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE=2048 (1024 for TI's peripheral sample), our BTHome beacon and TI's peripheral sample advertised. A Mac saw them. TI's beacon sample hard-faults. **Tag: Unknown.** Suspected: Tool or docs, the fork leaves the heap at 0 bytes

chains.t: Change settings without TI's setup app
chains.why: TI's SysConfig app writes the settings into a text file; we edited that file in a text editor instead. Four settings verified on the board; one option was ignored and had to be changed in C

benchmarks: CoreMark, TI Arm Clang -O3, bare metal
2.31 per MHz, 94% of Arm's figure for this core
CoreMark, Zephyr 4.4.2, GCC -O2 with loop unrolling
Also changes the OS and timer method; not a compiler-only comparison
20 commands, first pairing; about 5 s after re-pairing, cause unknown; the 2026-10-16 repeat did not join Home Assistant (cause open)
gotchas: Flashing fails with 'target failed to see a correctly formatted SWD header' (error -615)
**Tag: Unknown (suspected: Setup or handling).** Pull the probe off and press it back on
UniFlash says 'Unable to access the DAP'
a connection file written by hand leaves SWD off and this chip needs it on, so let CCStudio write the file, and check the command reaches the right probe (cc2340r5/FAQ.md)
TI's Zigbee example never joins Home Assistant
**Tag: TI example default.** It listens on channel 11 only; set all 16 channels
TI's log decoder prints 'unpack requires a buffer of 8 bytes'

change `struct.unpack("L", ts_format)` to `struct.unpack("<I", ts_format)` on line 132 of `tilogger_uart_transport/uart_to_log.py`; "L" is 4 bytes on Windows and 8 on macOS and Linux (cc2340r5/FAQ.md)
Zephyr's west flash does not work
**Tag: Third-party behavior.** This board's Zephyr setup knows only J-Link; flash with UniFlash

ai_cost.headline: A fresh AI agent with this repo's notes got Zephyr's blink running on this board in 3.0 to 3.6 minutes, for $0.12 to $1.36 of AI use at list price, depending on the model.

good_for: A Bluetooth device that talks to a computer: we tested from a Mac
A Zigbee light or switch in Home Assistant; its over-the-air update from Home Assistant stalled, see the experiments; the 2026-10-16 repeat did not join Home Assistant (cause open)
The Thread radio (RCP) for a Mac or another board that runs the Thread stack
Speed tests and plain C with no operating system
not_for: Thread nodes that run the network on the chip itself: TI's configurations did not link with our toolchain (not TI's tested one). They were 7.5 to 20.7 kB of RAM short for the default builds, and up to 23.8 kB with the NCP option. Suspected chip limit; a trimmed build was not tried
Matter: TI offers no Matter build for this chip
Two radio stacks at once: TI says CC23xx chips do not support it, and TI's two-radio example did not link here
A big app on top of a radio stack: about 5 kB of RAM is left with Bluetooth
Bluetooth under Zephyr: partly, in TI's fork only, with the C library heap set; one of TI's three samples faults

instead.why: 64 kB of RAM; TI's Thread end-device and router builds link for its chip, not run
TI's two-radio example links for its chip, not run
Matter over Thread, evaluation only; for Matter over Wi-Fi the LP-EM-CC35X1 has a production-ready release

buy: TI no longer sells this board on TI.com. The LP-EM-CC2340R53, $27.50 at TI.com, has the same radio and almost twice the RAM, 64 kB against 36 kB, so it is the one to buy. Both boards need a separate debug probe, such as the LP-XDS110ET, $59.29 at TI.com: $86.79 for the pair.
measured_on: Measured 2026-10-05 on an Intel Mac (macOS 15.7.9) with the SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36, SysConfig 1.26.3 and TI Arm Clang 5.1.1; Zephyr 4.4.2 with GCC 12.2.

hotspots.label: The chip
hotspots.title: CC2340R52
hotspots.text: A 48 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 512 kB of flash and 36 kB of RAM, and a 2.4 GHz radio for Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread and proprietary links. The antenna and its connector sit just above it.

hotspots.label: Debug header
hotspots.title: Header for the separate probe
hotspots.text: This board has no USB port. A separate XDS110 probe clips onto this header, which is marked with ground, 5V, 3V3, serial (RXD, TXD), reset and the SWD pins. The probe powers it, flashes it and carries the serial port.

hotspots.label: Headers
hotspots.title: BoosterPack pin headers
hotspots.text: Rows of numbered DIO pins run along the top and bottom edges, with 3V3, 5V and ground, for plug-on boards.

hotspots.label: LEDs
hotspots.title: Red and green LEDs
hotspots.text: The red LED (DIO14) is the one TI's SDK blink example toggles. The green one (DIO15) is the one Zephyr's blinky uses.
